papers.title: Acoustic assembly of cell spheroids in disposable capillaries.
papers.abstract: Multicellular spheroids represent a promising approach to mimic 3D tissues in vivo for emerging applications in regenerative medicine, therapeutic screening, and drug discovery. Conventional spheroid fabrication methods, such as the hanging drop method, suffer from low-throughput, long time, complicated procedure, and high heterogeneity in spheroid size. In this work, we report a simple yet reliable acoustic method to rapidly assemble cell spheroids in capillaries in a replicable and scalable manner. Briefly, by introducing a coupled standing surface acoustic wave, we are able to generate a linear pressure node array with 300 trapping nodes simultaneously. This enables us to continuously fabricate spheroids in a high-throughput manner with minimal variability in spheroid size. In a proof of concept application, we fabricated cell spheroids of mouse embryonic carcinoma (P19) cells, which grew well and retained differentiation potential in vitro. Based on the advantages of the non-invasive, contactless and label-free acoustic cell manipulation, our method employs the coupling strategy to assemble cells in capillaries, and further advances 3D spheroid assembly technology in an easy, cost-efficient, consistent, and high-throughput manner. This method could further be adapted into a novel 3D biofabrication approach to replicate compilated tissues and organs for a wide set of biomedical applications.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究声波组装细胞球体，未涉及任何人工智能技术，因此与AI生物打印研究方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper uses acoustic assembly for spheroid formation without any AI/ML integration, data-driven optimization, or autonomous decision-making in the bioprinting workflow.

summary_zh.motivation: 现有球体制造方法通量低、耗时长、异质性高。
summary_zh.method: 利用耦合驻波表面声波在毛细管内快速组装细胞球体。
summary_zh.result: 实现了高通量、一致性好的球体制造，细胞存活且保持分化能力。
summary_zh.validation: 使用小鼠胚胎癌P19细胞进行体外培养验证。

summary_en.motivation: Conventional spheroid fabrication methods suffer from low throughput, long processing time, and high size heterogeneity.
summary_en.method: A coupled standing surface acoustic wave (SAW) is introduced to generate a linear pressure node array in disposable capillaries for rapid, scalable spheroid assembly.
summary_en.result: The method enables continuous, high-throughput fabrication of uniform spheroids, with P19 cells showing good growth and retained differentiation potential.
summary_en.validation: In vitro culture of mouse embryonic carcinoma cells confirmed spheroid viability and function.

papers.title: F-doped TiO
papers.abstract: To enhance bacterial resistance and osteogenesis of titanium (Ti) -based implants, TiO2/calcium-phosphate coatings (TiCP) doped with various amounts of fluorine (F) (designated as TiCP-F1, TiCP-F6, and TiCP-F9) were prepared on Ti by micro-arc oxidation. The F doped TiCP coatings possess a microporous structure (pore size of 3-4 μm in average diameter) which is evenly covered by nano-grains of 30-60 nm in size. Successful F incorporation into TiCP was determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and it shows weak influence on the microstructure, phase compositions, surface roughness and wettability of TiCP. All the coatings bonded firmly to the Ti substrates and showed enduring high adhesion strength in biological circumstances. The bacterial resistance and osteogenesis of the coatings were evaluated by implanting testing materials in vitro and in an infected rabbit model caused by bacteria. Both the in vitro and in vivo results indicated that TiCP and TiCP-F1 were of much higher osteogenic activity compared with Ti but lacking of bacterial resistance, whereas TiCP with high F addition (TiCP-F6 and TiCP-F9) exhibited both dramatically improved bacterial resistance and osteogenesis. In summary, TiCP-F6 possessed the best antibacterial and osteogenic activities, especially exhibited excellent osseointegration efficacy in the infected rabbit model.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not involve additive manufacturing (LPBF), lacks mechanical testing (fatigue or compression), and does not address stress shielding or stiffness matching.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高钛植入体的抗菌和成骨性能
summary_zh.method: 通过微弧氧化在钛表面制备氟掺杂TiO2/钙磷涂层
summary_zh.result: 适量氟掺杂涂层兼具优异抗菌和成骨活性
summary_zh.validation: 体外细胞实验和兔感染模型体内验证

summary_en.motivation: To enhance bacterial resistance and osteogenesis of titanium-based implants.
summary_en.method: Fluorine-doped TiO2/calcium-phosphate coatings were fabricated on titanium via micro-arc oxidation.
summary_en.result: Coatings with appropriate fluorine content exhibited both improved antibacterial properties and osteogenic activity.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell assays and an infected rabbit model validated the dual functionality.
